days.lo: I am learning how to find and describe flat triangles, squares, rectangles, hexagons, and circles using informal language without naming them.
sc: I can describe the attributes of shapes.

days.lo: I am learning to explain decisions about classifications of triangles into categories using variants and non-examples and record on a picture graph. Identify shapes as triangles.
sc: I can sort triangles and non-triangles in groups.
I can describe my shape sort.
I can use math vocabulary to describe my shapes.

days.lo: I am learning to explain decisions about classifications of rectangles into categories using variants and non-examples and record on a picture graph. Identify shapes as rectangles.
sc: I can sort rectangles and non-rectangles in groups.
I can describe my shape sort.
I can use math vocabulary to describe my shapes.

days.lo: I am learning to explain decisions about classifications of hexagons and circles and identify them by name, and record on a picture graph.
sc: I can organize circles and hexagons on a bar graph.
I can describe the circles and hexagons.

days.lo: I am learning to describe and communicate positions of all flat shapes using the words above, below, beside, in front of, next to, and behind.
sc: I can identify two-dimensional shapes by their attributes.
I can describe the position of two-dimensional shapes.

days.lo: I am learning to find and describe solid shapes using informal language withoutnaming them.
sc: I can identify three-dimensional shapes around the classroom.
I can describe a solid shape using attributes.

days.lo: I am learning to explain decisions about classification of solid shapes intocategories and record on a picture graph.
sc: I can discuss classification of shapes.
I can create a picture graph from shape sort.
I can name the solid shapes.

days.lo: I am learning to describe and communicate positions of all solid shapes using the words above, below, beside, in front of, next to, and behind.
sc: I can identify the shapes by touch.
I can sort shapes in categories.

days.lo: I am learning to identify and sort shapes as two-dimensional or three-dimensional, and recognize two-dimensional and three-dimensional shapes in different orientations and sizes.
sc: I can identify the shapes from a bag.
I can name shapes.

End of Module 2 Assessment (review content 1 day, assessment 1-2 days, and/or remediation or further application 1 day)

days.lo: I am learning to compare lengths using taller than and shorter than with aligned and non-aligned endpoints.
sc: I can compare lengths using real life objects.
I can tell which objects are equal or the same length.

days.lo: I am learning to compare length measurements with string.
sc: I can compare lengths and heights with string.

days.lo: I am learning to make a series of longer than and shorter than comparisons.
sc: I can compare lengths that are shorter with a string.

days.lo: I am learning to compare the length of linking cube sticks to a 5-stick.
sc: I can compare lengths of linking cubes and a stick with different lengths.

days.lo: I am learning to determine which linking cube stick is longer than or shorter than the other.
sc: I can compare linking cubes or sticks side by side to find the longest and shortest.

days.lo: I am learning to compare the length of linking cube sticks to various objects.
sc: I can put number cubes in order from 1-10.
I can guess which real life objects might be longer or shorter than the measuring stick.

days.lo: I am learning to compare using heavier than and lighter than with classroom objects. I am learning to compare objects using heavier than, lighter than, and the same as with balance scales.
sc: I can compare weights of different objects in the classroom.
I can compare objects to find which object is heavier or lighter.
days.note: lessons combined (Lesson Highlights: notes on combining lessons; IPC lists only Lesson 8)

days.lo: I am learning to compare objects using heavier than, lighter than,and the same as with balance scales.
sc: I can compare weights using a balance scale.
I can describe something as heavier than, lighter than, or the same as.

days.lo: I am learning to compare the weight of an object to a set of unit weights on a balance scale.
sc: I can compare weights using a balance scale.
I can describe why something is heavier or lighter.

days.lo: I am learning how to observe the conservation of weight on the balance scale.
sc: I can describe how I know something is heavier or lighter.
I can observe that changing the shape of an object doesn’t change its weight.

days.lo: I am learning to compare the weight of an object with sets of different objects on a balance scale.
sc: I can compare weights of sets of objects.

days.lo: I am learning to compare volume using more than, less than, and the same as by pouring.
sc: I can find capacities that are more or less that others.
I can explore volume by pouring.
days.note: lessons combined (Lesson Highlights: notes on combining lessons; IPC lists only Lesson 13; Lesson 14 not scheduled)

days.lo: I am learning to compare using the same as with units.
sc: I can compare the capacity of items using the same units.

days.text: Mid-Module 3 Assessment (review content 1 day, assessment 1-2 days, and/or remediation or further application 1 day)
Mid-Module 3 Assessment (review content 1 day, assessment 1-2 days, and/or remediation or further application 1 day)

days.lo: I am learning to compare to find if there are enough.
sc: I can determine just enough, enough and not enough.

days.lo: I am learning to compare using more than and the same as.
sc: I can use the more than and same as to compare sets of objects.

days.lo: I am learning to compare using fewer than and the same as.
sc: I can use the fewer than and same as to compare sets of objects.

days.lo: I am learning to relate more and less to length.
sc: I can relate more to length.
I can relate less to length.

days.lo: I am learning to compare sets informally using more, less, and fewer.
sc: I can compare sets using the words more, less or fewer.

days.lo: I am learning to identify and create a set that has the same number of objects.
sc: I can identify a set that has the same number of objects.
I can create a set that has the same number of objects.

days.lo: I am learning to reason to identify and make a set that has 1 more.
sc: I can add one more to a set.

days.lo: I am learning to reason to identify and make a set that has 1 less.
sc: I can add one less to a set.

days.lo: I am learning to match and count to compare a number of objects and state which quantity is more.
sc: I can match objects.
I can count to compare objects.
I can state which set has more.

days.lo: I am learning to match and count to compare two sets of objects and state whichquantity is less.
sc: I can match two sets of objects.
I can count to compare two sets of objects.
I can say which set is less.

days.lo: I am learning to strategize to compare two sets.
sc: I can select a way to compare two sets of objects.

days.lo: I am learning to visualize quantities to compare two numerals.
sc: I can think of quantities to compare two numerals.
